Posted May 16, 2003
News and Analysis by Richard Cowan

Not to keep you in suspense, I am very optimistic about the outcome of Steve Tuck's refugee hearings, just as I was with the Kubby hearings.
See
 Tuck Refugee Hearings Begin. Canadian Government Brings In Heavy Artillery, Who Quickly Learn More Than They Wanted to Know. And I Play Lawyer. Special Report to MarijuanaNews by Richard Cowan
and links

As I reported Monday, we were allowed to keep the testimony from the Kubby hearings as part of the evidence in the Tuck case, and it will also be a part of the record for Ken Hayes hearings in July. Consequently, Tuck's hearings were shorter and less complicated than Kubby's.

There were no hearings yesterday, but on Wednesday, the Immigration Ministry called its only witness, Sergeant Wayne Hanson of the Humboldt County sheriff's department. (The testimony was by phone, but under oath.)

Sergeant Hanson testified that in his professional opinion the two grows which he raided had to be commercial, because they were too big and sophisticated to be medical.

Of course, no one could explain why the (former) District Attorney did not charge Tuck after either raid, despite the grows supposedly being too big and sophisticated to be medical. In fact, Tuck was not charged for anything until after he brought vandalism and other charges against Hanson and the (former) DA for wrecking his house on the second raid.

Hanson also insisted that the federal government would never bring charges against Tuck, but he said that he had not heard about San Diego medical cannabis activist Steve McWilliams, who is facing six months in the federal lock-up and three years of urine tested probation for 25 plants.
See
 Federal Prosecution of Activist Steve McWilliams For Just 25 Plants Relevant to American Refugees In Canada. Being Outspoken Is The Real Crime. Being Deprived Of Medication Is The Real Punishment.

Part of Hanson's testimony actually helped Tuck, inasmuch as he said that prisoners are not allowed to use medical cannabis in the Humboldt County jail, regardless of their condition. In fact, Hanson, a former Humboldt jailer, could not even assure the hearings that Tuck would be allowed to use morphine prescribed for pain. However, he did make the medical care at the Humboldt jail sound slightly better than Mayo Clinic.

He also said that if Tuck were to return to Humboldt he would be arrested and held on a substantial bail. If Tuck is not allowed to use cannabis and morphine, he would die in indescribable pain. It was that threat that sent him fleeing for his life to Canada.

Hanson also helped Tuck's case when I asked him to explain the total incompatibility of the old and new District Attorneys Guidelines for growing medical cannabis in Humboldt County. His response was simply that it was all political the difference between a Republican and a Democrat.

He also could not explain how either version was related to Prop 215, the Compassionate Use Act. The old Guidelines actually required that the Caregivers live with the patients, which is patently absurd.
See
 What Part Of 'Exempt' Do California District Attorneys Still Not Understand?

My last question to Hanson concerned the condition of the Tuck's houses after the raids. He said that there was nothing unusual about the condition of either house, except that Steve had damaged the second house when he put in the lights. That seems odd for something so sophisticated, but he had a reason for saying that

Today, we called our only witness, the well-known private investigator, Daniel Weaver of Petrolia, California. Weaver was one of only two witnesses allowed to testify for the defense at the Ed Rosenthal trial. His resume runs for several pages.
See
 DEAland On Trial At Kubby Refugee Hearings. Damning Testimony From A Patient, A Judge and Ed Rosenthal. Meanwhile, Congress Was Busy Making It Even Worse. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com
and links

Weaver has examined over 400 marijuana cultivation sites involving more than 50,000 plants. He said that he had never seen anything like the damage to the Tucks home after the second raid. He called it vandalism. I asked him if the damage could have been done by Tuck when he installed the lights, and he explained that the worst damage was in a study where there were no plants. The Tucks personal possessions were dumped in a stack that was taller than he is. Family photos were ground into the floor, the frames and glass broken and scattered everywhere.

In fact, the veteran investigator was so disturbed by the wanton destruction of the Tucks home that he did not charge the Tucks for his investigation, and said that he was ashamed of what his country was doing to people like them.

In response to questions by the Immigration Ministry, he said that he thought that the grows were obviously medical rather than commercial because Steve had grown a wide variety of plants, which were labeled and identified for specific medical uses. He also noted that commercial grows tend to concentrate on just a few strains and are set up to maximize the yield, which these were not.

He also testified that Steve is well-known in Humboldt County for his medical marijuana activism.

On that note, the hearings ended and a ruling is expected in November. Will Canada send the refugees back to die? Frankly, I don't think so, but giving them refugee status is going to cause yet another rift with DEAland over cannabis policy, and is one more reason that Canada desperately needs to have a national debate on cannabis prohibition.

Canada must confront the prohibitionist hyperpower that fears nothing more than truth and freedom.
See
 How Canada Could Have A Major Impact On The World By Legalizing Cannabis. More Than Its Own Sovereignty Is At Stake. What Washington Really Fears Is Freedom. Supreme Court Cases Make This Urgent.

Of the many blessings of my life, nothing equals the great joy and honor of being able to play a small part in helping my friends defend their lives and liberty. I am so grateful to God and so ashamed of my country.
